title: Co-ordinate Geometry
summary: Two perpendicular number lines, the x-axis and the y-axis, meet at the origin O(0, 0). A point is written (x, y): x (abscissa) is its distance from the y-axis and y (ordinate) its distance from the x-axis, with signs. So P(−2, 3) is 2 units from the y-axis and 3 units from the x-axis. Every point on the x-axis has y = 0, and every point on the y-axis has x = 0.
The axes divide the plane into four quadrants: I (+, +), II (−, +), III (−, −), IV (+, −). (4, −2) lies in quadrant IV, (−5, 2) in II, and (0, −4) is not in any quadrant — it lies on the y-axis.

The distance between A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) is AB = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]. From the origin: √(x² + y²). Example: (2, −2) and (−1, x) are 5 apart ⇒ 9 + (x + 2)² = 25 ⇒ x = 2 or −6. Use it to find radii (centre to a point on the circle), perimeters, to test the type of a triangle, and to show three points are collinear (the two shorter distances add up to the longest).

The point dividing the join of A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) internally in the ratio m : n is ((mx₂ + nx₁)/(m + n), (my₂ + ny₁)/(m + n)). The midpoint (ratio 1 : 1) is ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2). To find the ratio in which an axis divides AB, take the ratio k : 1 and put the x-coordinate (y-axis) or the y-coordinate (x-axis) equal to 0.
The medians of a triangle meet at the centroid G, which divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1. For vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃): G = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃)/3).
## Area of a triangle (used in past papers)
Area = ½ |x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|. If the area is 0 the points are collinear. A quadrilateral's area is found by splitting it into two triangles along a diagonal.

Write True or False (any two): (i) (0, −4) lies in quadrant IV. (ii) The distance of (2, −3) from the x-axis is 3. (iii) The midpoint of (1, 0) and (3, −2) is (−2, −1). (iv) A circle with centre O through (2, −3) has radius √13.

(i) False: x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis.
(ii) True: |y| = 3.
(iii) False: ((1 + 3)/2, (0 − 2)/2) = (2, −1).
(iv) True: √(2² + 3²) = √13.
Write True or False: (i) R(−2, −3) lies in quadrant III. (ii) The point (0, 5) lies on the x-axis.

(i) True: both coordinates are negative.
(ii) False: x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis.

vsa: Find a point on the x-axis which is equidistant from (7, 6) and (−3, 4).

Let it be P(x, 0). PA² = PB²: (x − 7)² + 36 = (x + 3)² + 16.
x² − 14x + 85 = x² + 6x + 25 ⇒ 20x = 60 ⇒ x = 3.

sa: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the join of (4, −5) and (−1, 2). Also find the point of division.

Let the ratio be k : 1. x-coordinate of the point = (k(−1) + 1 × 4)/(k + 1) = 0 (on the y-axis) ⇒ −k + 4 = 0 ⇒ k = 4.
Ratio 4 : 1.
y = (4 × 2 + 1 × (−5))/5 = 3/5. The point is (0, 3/5).

or: Show that A(1, 5), B(7, −1) and C(4, 2) are collinear.

AC = √[(4 − 1)² + (2 − 5)²] = √18 = 3√2.
CB = √[(7 − 4)² + (−1 − 2)²] = √18 = 3√2.
AB = √[(7 − 1)² + (−1 − 5)²] = √72 = 6√2.
AC + CB = 6√2 = AB, so the points are collinear (C lies between A and B — in fact it is the midpoint).

Prove that O(0, 0), A(4, 3) and B(8, 6) are collinear.

OA = √(16 + 9) = 5; AB = √(16 + 9) = 5; OB = √(64 + 36) = 10.
OA + AB = 10 = OB, so the three points are collinear.

Find the area of the triangle with vertices A(3, 0), B(7, 0) and C(8, 4).

A and B lie on the x-axis, so base AB = 4 and height = y-coordinate of C = 4.
Area = ½ × 4 × 4 = 8 sq units.
(Formula: ½|3(0 − 4) + 7(4 − 0) + 8(0 − 0)| = ½|−12 + 28| = 8.)

Find the area of the rhombus with vertices A(3, 0), B(4, 5), C(−1, 4) and D(−2, −1). Also find the distance between its sides AB and CD.

Diagonals: AC = √[(−1 − 3)² + (4 − 0)²] = √32 = 4√2; BD = √[(−2 − 4)² + (−1 − 5)²] = √72 = 6√2.
Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 4√2 × 6√2 = 24 sq units.
Side AB = √(1 + 25) = √26. A rhombus is a parallelogram, so area = base × height:
24 = √26 × h ⇒ h = 24/√26 ≈ 4.71 units — the distance between AB and CD.
